sources.used_for: Every daily price on the site: the C6 chart, drawdown and volatility, and the last close behind the C7.5 maths

discrepancies.versions: ~3.3–4× ($250bn book vs $75bn raise, by 9 June) vs nearer 2× in some later reporting
discrepancies.treatment: Both shown in C5; neither hidden.
The C4 duel uses $236 with the $188 figure and full range noted alongside.

discrepancies.versions: $1.77tn offering valuation vs ~$2.1tn day-one market cap — different share-count bases
discrepancies.treatment: The Position (C7.5) states which base its implied-growth maths uses.

discrepancies.versions: $225.64 (+67%) is the widely reported peak, but it was an intraday high on 16 June; the highest close was $211.39 the same day. The ~32% give-back is measured from the intraday high; on closes it is ~31%.
discrepancies.treatment: Headline figures quote the reported intraday peak; the C6 chart plots closes and labels its peak as a close.

assumptions: Prices are live Yahoo Finance data, deliberately cut at the 10 July close: the site is a dated July snapshot and The Position is on the record as of 11 July.
The supply schedule between the reported endpoints (4% at IPO, ~40% by December) is an estimate interpolated from reported lockup terms — labelled as such on the chart.
The C5 intraday line connects only the four reported session anchors; no intraday path is invented between them.

Implied-growth maths uses the $1.77tn offering-valuation share base scaled by the latest price (see the valuation-vs-market-cap discrepancy above), 2025 adjusted EBITDA of $6.6bn, and a 5-year horizon to 2030.
